$ASML is one of the cleanest ways to own the AI semiconductor buildout because every major chip trend ultimately requires lithography.

Memory rose to 51% of net system sales in Q1 2026 (up from 30% in Q4) while the average EUV system price has nearly doubled in five years as customers move toward more advanced tools.

As $MU, $SKHY and Samsung expand HBM and advanced DRAM capacity, ASML benefits upstream without needing to pick which memory supplier wins the most share.

$ORCL profits are expected to triple over the next three years while the stock trades below 10x 2029 earnings with OCI growing 93% and backlog reaching ~$640B.

If $META and OpenAI demand turns that backlog into revenue then Oracle could emerge as the fourth major AI cloud before the market fully prices it in.

Goldman Sachs expects $SPCX Starship AI missions to reach 5,288 by 2031 with each carrying 30–50 satellites powered by one GB300-equivalent rack apiece.

That could mean millions of accelerators from $NVDA, fabricated by $TSM with $MU & $SKHY supplying the HBM behind each rack.
Wild to see $MU posting higher operating margins than $NVDA... shows how AI has made memory bandwidth even scarcer than compute design.

THE MOST PROFITABLE AI SEMICONDUCTOR STOCKS

Operating margin breakdown:
• Best-in-class (50%+) | $MU, $NVDA, $SKHY, $TSM 
• Elite (40–49%) | $ANET, $AVGO, $KLAC, $SNDK

$SKHY DRAM revenue has risen more than 5x in three years as AI demand shifted from H100 clusters to memory-heavy $NVDA Blackwell systems.

HBM eats 2 to 3x the silicon per gigabyte so every wafer redirected to feed Blackwell removed 3x that in commodity DRAM turning memory bandwidth into the binding constraint on intelligence.

The chip is slated for future Tesla products with volume production expected later.

A bullish setup for me is when the 9-day EMA is above the 21-day EMA & the stock is holding both the 50-day & 200-day SMA so both momentum + structure are moving in the same direction.

If the only level a stock is holding is the 200-day SMA then the long-term trend is still intact but the momentum has faded so I treat it as a hold.

When the price breaks below all three levels then that is when I consider the trend bearish because the short-term, intermediate & long-term signals are all pointing the same way.
